subject: DPA: model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response custody and cross-border subprocessors
messages:
From: Elisa Tran <e.tran@novum-health.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@novum-health.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA wording — model improvement and prompt/response custody

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the DPA draft. Two quick but important asks from our legal and privacy teams before we move to countersign:

1) We need an explicit "no model-improvement" commitment for our tenant data (we call this no-adaptive-training). Can Redwood confirm a contractual prohibition on using our prompts/responses to improve any models or train internal model variants?

2) Clarify ownership/custody language: our legal wants the DPA to explicitly state that prompts and responses (including derived logs) remain Novum Health customer data and are not licensed for downstream productization.

Additional practical question: if Redwood uses subprocessors for embeddings or vector DBs in different regions, what controls exist to prevent cross-border processing that would violate our EU residency requirement?

Appreciate a short note addressing all three points and a suggested next step (redlines we should expect or an ops checklist).

Best,
Elisa
Elisa Tran
Head of Privacy, Novum Health

From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elisa Tran <e.tran@novum-health.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording — model improvement and prompt/response custody

Hi Elisa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (privacy/legal) and Kimberly (ops) who will help with the technical/control responses. High-level answers while they prepare redlines:

- No-model-improvement: Redwood can commit to a contractual prohibition on using tenant prompts/responses for any model training or improvement of public/hosted models. We typically offer a carveout for "explicit, opt-in pilot programs" only if agreed separately and with customer consent.

- Data custody: We can add language that prompts/responses and derived logs are customer data and cannot be repurposed as product training data or licensed to third parties. We'll propose exact wording for clarity around "derived analytics" vs. product telemetry.

- Subprocessors & cross-border: We have an approved subprocessor inventory and can commit to EU-only processing for this account when specified in the DPA. David/Kimberly — can you confirm the routing guarantees and how we bound subprocessor transfers (SFTP/on-prem, onshore vector stores, KMS residency)?

Elisa — I'll follow up with a redline and an ops checklist within 24 hours, and include our subprocessor inventory as requested.

Thanks,
Grace Oconnor
Director, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: request noted (we will attach subprocessor inventory and DPA redline)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Elisa Tran <e.tran@novum-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording — model improvement and prompt/response custody

Hi all — short technical/legal confirmation from my side:

1) Contract language we propose: 
   - "Provider shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, and any derived interaction logs) to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning model, internal or external, unless Customer provides prior written consent for a specific, time-bounded pilot."
   - That phrasing is intentionally broad — it covers both model training and downstream use for productization.

2) Prompt/response custody vs. telemetry: we recommend adding a definition block: "Customer Data = raw prompts, responses, and explicitly related transaction logs; Telemetry = anonymized service health metrics. Provider may collect telemetry solely for operational purposes and in aggregated/anonymized form; telemetry does not include Customer Data."

3) Subprocessor & cross-border controls: operational commitments we can make in the DPA (to be reflected in the redline):
   - EU-only processing clause for the Novum tenant (no transfer outside EU without Customer's written approval).
   - Subprocessor gating: any subprocessor with access to Customer Data must be in our approved EU subprocessor list; new subprocessors require 30 days' notice and a right to object.
   - KMS residency: keys for Novum can be bound to EU-region KMS; we will include an optional onshore-KMS addendum.

I attached a draft redline and the current EU subprocessor spreadsheet for review (see attachments). Kimberly, please add the runbook steps for SFTP and vector-store isolation.

-David
David Kim
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: DPA_redline_model-improvement_20270610.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20270610.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elisa Tran <e.tran@novum-health.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA wording — model improvement and prompt/response custody

Hi Elisa — following up with the ops commitments and next steps.

Summary of attachments and controls (attached PDFs/Excel):
- DPA_redline_model-improvement_20270610.pdf: includes the proposed contractual no-training clause, Customer Data definition, and an EU-only processing addendum.
- subprocessor_inventory_20270610.xlsx: current list with region and access level; marked EU-only options.

Operational controls we will execute once DPA is signed:
- Tenant routing: traffic for Novum will be pinned to our EU inference cluster; embeddings and vector storage will be provisioned in the EU cluster by default.
- KMS binding: offer option for Novum-managed KMS or Redwood-managed EU KMS with strict key separation.
- Subprocessor gating: 30-day notice window and a documented objection process.
- Audit evidence: we can provide a snapshot of subprocessor access logs and a 3-month retention export for initial attestation.

Action items / ask from Novum:
1) Confirm the proposed redline (attached) or provide any specific phrasing changes by EOD Tue, Jun 15.
2) If you require a customer-managed KMS, let us know and we'll schedule a short runbook call (30m).
3) Sign the Docusign link when ready; we've set up the envelope under DEAL-78321 (link below).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/novum-dpa-78321

If helpful, I can join a short call with your privacy counsel to walk through the redline — available Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
